_note: v2 hook overrides for l'Hôpital (B19_hopital). Source hooks are kept where the painting shows them; these replace hooks whose painted scene differs, mostly to avoid repeated animals across the six rooms. Medical content is gentle: no blood; needles appear only as one big wooden toy syringe; déjection is a blank plaque.

fr_hopital_noun.hook: A TALL nurse on stilts ("oh-pea-TAHL", no S and no H) hands a boy in a wheelchair a flower PETAL from her rose as he arrives at the HOSPITAL.
fr_hopital_noun.why: Matches the painting: she gives him a rose petal; the box marks the stilts nurse.

fr_miracle_noun.hook: A MIRACLE ("mee-RAHKL"): a dry old rose bush by the hospital wall has burst into flower overnight.
fr_miracle_noun.why: No bench is painted beside the rose bush; it climbs the wall by the stairs.

fr_dommage_noun.hook: A toy robot with a dented arm waits by the fountain to be mended: what DAMAGE ("doh-MAHZH"), what a shame!
fr_dommage_noun.why: No nurse stands next to the robot, so the hook rests on the dented toy alone.

fr_asile_noun.hook: A robin family finds ASYLUM in a snug nest box, welcomed with ZEAL ("ah-ZEEL") by a gardener who holds the box up high under the palms.

fr_operation_noun.hook: A surgeon sings OPERA ("oh-pay-rah-SYOHN") behind a half-open green curtain during a teddy's OPERATION, gently mending his arm.
fr_operation_noun.why: Kept gentle: the teddy is being mended, no stitching shown.

fr_aide_noun_f.hook: A kind nurse's assistant opens a red first-AID kit to HELP a boy with a grazed knee, his TEDDY ("ehd") holding the box of plasters.
fr_aide_noun_f.why: Matches the painting; 'aide' here is the help / the (woman) assistant.

fr_chirurgien_noun.hook: The SURGEON ("shee-rewr-ZHYAN") in a green cap scrubs her hands at a little sink, humming two whole songs.
fr_chirurgien_noun.why: Painted as a little figurine on the tray, a lady surgeon at a sink.

fr_injection_noun.hook: A brave puppy hugs a giant wooden toy syringe, bigger than himself: his INJECTION ("an-zhehk-SYOHN") is over and he is very proud.
fr_injection_noun.why: Kept gentle: one big friendly wooden toy syringe and a proud puppy, no nurse and no real needle.

fr_detachement_noun.hook: A calm grey cat with a white MOUSTACHE ("day-tah-shuh-MAHN") washes a paw beside the goat's mess, watching it all with DETACHMENT.
fr_detachement_noun.why: Matches the painting: the cat sits right next to the torn towels.

fr_operateur_noun.hook: The OPERATOR ("oh-pay-rah-TUHR"), a technician in a blue cap, swings the big round theatre lamp into place.
fr_operateur_noun.why: He wears a plain blue cap, so the 'tour guide' detail is dropped.

fr_piqure_noun.hook: A curious bee, a little PEEKER ("pea-KEWR"), peeks at the tiny STING on a boy's arm while he holds an ice cube on it.
fr_piqure_noun.why: The boy holds the ice cube himself; no nurse on the tray.

fr_chirurgie_noun.hook: SHE ("shee-rewr-ZHEE"), a girl in a paper cap, does SURGERY on her teddy's ear, steady as a pro.

fr_exploitation_noun.hook: A hen manager runs the hospital laundry OPERATION ("ehk-splwah-tah-SYOHN") with a clipboard, sheets hanging on the line behind her.

fr_degat_noun.hook: DAMAGE! one DAY ("day") a GOAT ("GAH") wandered in and chewed the mop, leaving a puddle on the floor.
fr_degat_noun.why: The torn paper towels lie by the cat next door; the goat and the puddle carry the hook.

fr_interruption_noun.hook: A toddler in pyjamas toots a toy trumpet: an INTERRUPTION ("an-teh-rewp-SYOHN") right in the middle of the doctor's round.
fr_interruption_noun.why: Painted as a toddler with a trumpet, not a duck, because the ducks already carry l'évacuation.

fr_infirmerie_noun.hook: IN FEAR ("an-feer-muh-REE"), little MARY brings her rag doll to the INFIRMARY, where a nurse bandages its arm.
fr_infirmerie_noun.why: A rag doll instead of a teddy, so the upstairs ward does not repeat the teddies of the entrance hall.

fr_sauvetage_noun.hook: A lifeguard who SAVED ("soh-vuh") a little swimmer carries him in his arms, the boy still hugging his red float: a RESCUE.
fr_sauvetage_noun.why: He carries the swimmer instead of wheeling him, so the ward has only one wheelchair (le handicap).

fr_derision_noun.hook: A pompous crow sings by the bed, and two parrots on the bed rail hoot with DERISION ("day-ree-ZYOHN").
fr_derision_noun.why: The box marks the two laughing parrots; the crow sits a little further left with its music notes.

fr_anesthesie_noun.hook: Under ANAESTHESIA ("-ZEE") a koala sleeps deeply on a soft round cushion, dreaming of eucalyptus.
fr_anesthesie_noun.why: Painted as a koala with no ZZZ letters (no text in the paintings) and no bear, because a bear already does la récupération.

fr_recuperation_noun.hook: A grandpa in a dressing gown does slow RECOVERY ("ray-kew-pay-rah-SYOHN") exercises, lifting a teaCUP like a dumbbell.
fr_recuperation_noun.why: animal sweep: animal replaced by a person

fr_entorse_noun.hook: A footballer's ankle twisted IN TORSION ("ahn-TORS"): a SPRAIN, resting on a bed wrapped in a big blue ice pack.

fr_veterinaire_noun.hook: VET TERRY ("vay-tay-ree-NEHR") leans NEAR a nervous hamster in a tiny bed, listening with her stethoscope.

fr_scanner_noun.hook: A girl slides into the big doughnut SCANNER ("skah-NEHR") as the screen fills with friendly bones.
fr_scanner_noun.why: The patient is a girl, so the hamster appears only once (le vétérinaire).

fr_prothese_noun.hook: A smiling runner jogs past on a shiny curved PROSTHESIS ("proh-TEHZ") blade.

fr_reanimation_noun.hook: The heartbeat line on the monitor bounces back up like a RE-ANIMATED ("ray-ah-nee-mah-SYOHN") cartoon, and the bunny in the bed wakes up smiling in INTENSIVE CARE.
fr_reanimation_noun.why: A bunny instead of a teddy, to avoid repeating the teddies.

fr_infiltration_noun.hook: Rain INFILTRATES ("an-feel-trah-SYOHN") through a crack in the little roof and drips through a FILTER funnel into a bucket: an INFILTRATION.
fr_infiltration_noun.why: Shown as water seeping in, the word's everyday meaning, so no syringe is painted (needles kept sparing).

fr_dejection_noun.hook: Said day-zhehk-SYOHN: a small blank brass plaque on the tray's rim stands for DÉJECTION, a formal word for droppings; a false friend, not English 'dejection'.
fr_dejection_noun.why: Shown only as a blank plaque, with no writing and nothing else painted.

fr_insertion_noun.hook: A nurse makes a neat INSERTION ("an-sehr-SYOHN"), slipping a fresh page into a chart binder.

fr_prejudice_noun.hook: A toy football has knocked a flowerpot over and spilt its soil: PRAY, JUDGE ("pray-zhew-DEES") the HARM done!
fr_prejudice_noun.why: No nurse is painted; the ball and tipped pot carry the hook.

fr_ambulancier_noun.hook: A PARAMEDIC in a yellow jacket wheels the AMBULANCE ("ahn-bew-lahn-SYAY") stretcher with a smiling piglet aboard.
fr_ambulancier_noun.why: A piglet instead of a teddy, to avoid repeating the teddies.

fr_dam_noun.hook: A beaver holds his little twig DAM that burst, water dripping into a puddle: to his great DISMAY and HARM.
fr_dam_noun.why: Matches the painting; the only beaver in the building.

fr_dentiste_noun.hook: The DENTIST ("dahn-TEEST") polishes a giggling boy's teeth, and he squirms as if he's being TEASED.
fr_dentiste_noun.why: animal sweep: animal replaced by a person

fr_reflexe_noun.hook: An old doctor taps a boy's knee, and the REFLEX ("ray-FLEHKS") kick FLEXES his leg and sends a slipper flying.
fr_reflexe_noun.why: animal sweep: animal replaced by a person

fr_interlocuteur_noun.hook: A man in a bowler hat chats with his INTERLOCUTOR ("an-tehr-loh-kew-TUHR"), a jolly lady who answers every question with her mouth wide open.
fr_interlocuteur_noun.why: animal sweep: animal replaced by a person

fr_fente_noun.hook: A tiny FAWN ("FAHNT") peers through the narrow SLIT between the slats of the crate, its big eye in the CRACK.
fr_fente_noun.why: The slit is in the rooster's crate, not a shutter.

fr_illusion_noun.hook: A spiral card makes an optical ILLUSION ("ee-lew-ZYOHN"), and the man holding it stares, spellbound.

fr_correspondance_noun.hook: A postbag of CORRESPONDENCE ("koh-rehs-pohn-DAHNS") spills open by the waiting bench, and the letters DANCE out.

fr_lentille_noun.hook: An old lady scientist holds up a big LENS shaped like a giant LENTIL ("lahn-TEEY").
fr_lentille_noun.why: An old lady scientist instead of a mouse, so the mice stay with le réflexe.

fr_iris_noun.hook: A lemur looks through a big brass lens that makes its golden IRIS ("ee-REES") huge, a purple iris flower tucked behind its ear.
fr_iris_noun.why: A lemur instead of a cat, to avoid repeating the cat.

fr_dentaire_adj.hook: A little girl in a yellow apron polishes a big DENTAL model of teeth ("dahn-TEHR") on the low table until every tooth shines.
fr_dentaire_adj.why: A squirrel instead of a mouse, so the mice are not repeated.

fr_optique_adj.hook: A curly-haired boy peers through a big brass OPTICAL lens ("op-TEEK") — his eye meets a lemur's enormous eye on the other side.

fr_girofle_noun.hook: A GIRAFFE ("zhee-ROFL") leans in through the open door to nibble a single CLOVE held out by the lady dentist (clove oil soothes toothache).

fr_microscope_noun.hook: A moustached police COP ("mee-krohs-KOP") in a blue cap peers into a brass MICROSCOPE.
fr_microscope_noun.why: animal sweep: animal replaced by a person

fr_prescription_noun.hook: In his brand-new PRESCRIPTION glasses ("prehs-kreep-SYOHN") a little boy beside the big brass telescope sees the starry sky clearly for the first time.
fr_prescription_noun.why: animal sweep: animal replaced by a person

fr_lunette_noun.hook: "lew-NEHT": LUNAR NETS! In the basket lie GLASSES whose lenses are two little crescent MOONS: LUNAR specs, les lunettes.
fr_lunette_noun.why: la lunette = telescope; les lunettes = glasses. The loon in a net acts out the sound; the glasses give the meaning, in the optician's room.

fr_paupiere_noun.hook: A sleepy girl's EYELIDS droop shut as she sniffs a red POPPY ("poh-PYEHR").
fr_paupiere_noun.why: animal sweep: owl replaced by a girl
